page: Microsoft Azure DC16as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine engineered within the DCASv5 series, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor delivering 16 dedicated virtual cores derived from 8 physical cores via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 64.0 GB of RAM, sustaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per thread. The processor architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache pool. Supported instruction sets encompass AVX, FMA, BMI2, ADX, and specialized cryptographic primitives such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, while AVX-512 extensions are absent.

The instance features no bundled local disk storage or integrated GPUs, requiring attached remote network volumes for persistent operating system and data requirements. It supports Premium Storage integration to deliver consistent disk I/O over the storage fabric. In standard benchmark testing, the DC16as_v5 delivers consistent middle-tier scores across all evaluated metrics. It demonstrates a PassMark CPU score of 17,113.51, a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,324.0, and 15,871.18 on multi-core stress-ng tests. In data-centric evaluations, the instance records 5,880.38 on PassMark database operations and achieves 13.93 million operations per second on Redis SET operations, reflecting balanced core-to-memory throughput.

Because storage must be provided via remote volumes and no public IPv4 addresses are bundled natively, network architecture and persistent disk latency must be accounted for in production topologies. Cost efficiency remains tied to its balanced 1:4 configuration, preventing over-provisioning when compute and RAM demands scale uniformly. The DC16as_v5 is well matched for mid-sized relational database servers utilizing managed remote disks, enterprise application backends, containerized microservices, CI/CD compilation tasks, and standard business workloads requiring dedicated x86 execution threads.
description: Microsoft Azure DC16as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DCASv5 family. Built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provisions 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware incorporates instruction set extensions including AES, VAES, SHA-NI, AVX, and BMI2, though it lacks AVX-512 support. The server includes no bundled local disk storage or integrated GPUs, necessitating remote premium storage attachments for data persistence. Across benchmark evaluations, the DC16as_v5 achieves middle-tier results, reaching a PassMark CPU score of 17,113.51 and handling 13.93 million Redis SET operations per second. This profile suits balanced production workloads including enterprise web services, relational databases with remote storage, and secure business applications.
